summary: Morning timeout spike causing streaming disconnects and quota surges for VeloxHealth — post-incident action plan
description: Issue summary: During VeloxHealth's scheduled morning ETL (08:30–09:15 ET) on 2026-03-10, customers observed a sudden spike in request timeouts and streaming disconnects resulting in 5xx responses and elevated token billing. Impact: production traffic for VeloxHealth experienced degraded end-to-end latency (p95 increased from 220ms to 2.1s) and ~18% request failure rate for 45 minutes.
timeline: 2026-03-10 08:28 ET: VeloxHealth runs bulk job that ramps traffic to Redwood API
2026-03-10 08:31 ET: Monitoring alerts — streaming disconnects rise; api-gateway 5xx rate increases
2026-03-10 08:33 ET: Automatic reroute to fallback model pool kicks in (latency reduces for some requests)
2026-03-10 08:40 ET: Support triage; SRE increases autoscaler target and initiates emergency scale-up
2026-03-10 09:12 ET: Traffic returns to expected patterns after scale and manual cache flush; rate of errors drops below baseline
steps_to_reproduce: 1) From a client in us-east-1, issue concurrent streaming generation requests at burst rate comparable to VeloxHealth ETL (simulated 1.5–2x steady-state QPS)
2) Ensure requests pin to redwood-llama-13b-v2 and include long-context prompts (>=2048 tokens)
3) Observe increased tail latency in the serving-runtime and occasional gRPC stream resets from api-gateway
logs: api-gateway: 2026-03-10T08:31:12Z ERROR stream_reset code=14 upstream_timeout service=redwood-gateway request_id=abc123
serving-runtime: 2026-03-10T08:32:05Z WARN kv-cache-miss rate=0.74 seq_len=2048 pool=dedicated-13b
autoscaler: 2026-03-10T08:35:47Z INFO scale_up triggered from 12 -> 28 GPUs (scale delay 45s)
temporary_mitigation: 1) Enabled emergency burst capacity for VeloxHealth dedicated pool (+50% for 30 minutes)
2) Applied an automated per-customer rate cap to smooth ingress and avoid billing overrun
3) Flushed prefix cache for affected model pool to reduce KV conflict on heavily cached prefixes
investigation_notes: Initial hypothesis: autoscaler reaction time and GPU allocation led to queued requests and gRPC timeouts at the gateway layer.
SRE found hotspot: high-pressure long-context requests caused disproportionate KV cache churn and degraded kernel scheduling efficiency on the 13B pool.

Secondary factor: a recently-deployed kernel-selection heuristic (PR #3124) biased toward a slower but more memory-efficient kernel for certain sequence-lengths, increasing per-token latency under high concurrency.
Billing spike: temporary reroutes to higher-cost fallback variants plus replayed client retries contributed to bill variance for VeloxHealth during the incident.
resolution: Rollout of a two-part fix: (1) Reverted the kernel-selection heuristic from PR #3124 for redwood-llama-13b-v2 in prod pools serving enterprise customers; (2) Tuned autoscaler policy to reduce scale-up delay and increase warm capacity for predictable scheduled bursts. Both changes were deployed to prod us-east-1 and monitored for 48 hours. Customer was refunded for excess billing due to retry amplification and excess fallback usage.
action_items: A1: Engineering to add a scheduled-burst knob (feature request) so customers can declare daily heavy windows; ETA Q2 2026 — owner: Diego Alvarez
A2: Runtime team to add a fast-path kernel for long-context workloads and include load-based fallback thresholds — ETA 3 weeks — owner: Priya Menon
A3: Observability: add prefix/KV cache contention metric and a dedicated alert with runbook — ETA 1 week — owner: SRE team
A4: CS & Billing: issue customer credit and review billing thresholds; document guidance for customers running large ETL bursts — owner: Maya Patel — done
A5: Postmortem page and summary sent to VeloxHealth and #support; schedule 1:1 follow-up within 5 business days — owner: Customer Success
